notes.text: Erik Gustafsson is out 2-4 weeks and missed their last game. He is a top-pair defenseman. Brian Dumoulin has taken his spot beside Brandt Clarke.
Artemi Panarin returned in their last game after missing 4 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 20% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
A.J. Greer is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 12 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Leo Carlsson is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward.
Stian Solberg was added to the roster on Nov 21 and has played beside Tristan Luneau.

stakes: The Kings go in seventh in the Pacific with 18 points, 7 points behind the Ducks, third.

ANA.head: A genuine toss-up
ANA.body: Los Angeles has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Anaheim has home-ice advantage. The Ducks can tip it if they keep the shots coming.

LAK.head: A genuine toss-up
LAK.body: Los Angeles has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Anaheim has home-ice advantage. For the Kings, the difference could be keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: Malott meets his old team
paras: The Kings (8-12-2) beat Montréal 2-1 on Monday, and the Ducks (12-13-1) beat San Jose 7-0 on Wednesday. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Kings seventh (30th in the NHL) and the Ducks third (20th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Kings have played better than their record (.409) says: their chances are worth about .596, and their finishing has held them back. The Ducks’ record (.481) is about what their chances are worth.

The Kings leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest), keep dangerous shots away better than anyone (1st) and hound the puck on the forecheck (4th). The Ducks, by contrast, give up a lot of dangerous shots (31st). They also have had shaky goaltending (29th). Anaheim has scored 3.69 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. The Ducks are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Kings. On top of that, both teams like to hit, especially the Ducks (3rd), so expect plenty of it.

Artemi Panarin (8 G / 12 A / 20 P in 18 GP) leads the Kings in scoring, with a point in six straight games against Anaheim. Alex Laferriere (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Ducks, Cutter Gauthier (23 G / 9 A / 32 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Mikael Granlund (8 G / 21 A / 29 P in 25 GP) isn’t far behind.
Darcy Kuemper (8-5-1 / .891 SV% in 14 GS) is expected to start for Los Angeles, and Laurent Brossoit (5-1-0 / .887 SV% in 6 GS) for Anaheim.
